replies.body:
>(a) VirtualField registration under javaagent:
>
TracingFilter (in library-autoconfigure) is transitively referenced through the helper class chain: `OpenTelemetryClientFilter → SofaRpcSingletons.clientFilter() → SofaRpcTelemetry.build() → new TracingFilter(...)`. The javaagent's HelperClassFinder recursively follows all class references from the declared exposedClassNames, so TracingFilter is included in the helper class set. The VirtualFieldImplementationInstaller scans bytecode of all helper classes for `VirtualField.find(X.class, Y.class)` calls, which means it should detect the `VirtualField.find(SofaRequest.class, Context.class)` declaration and properly register the field injection for SofaRequest.
>
> (b) Async test coverage:
>
The AbstractSofaRpcTest base class includes async client test cases that exercise the request.isAsync() == true branch. SofaRpcAgentTest extends this base class, so the async path is exercised under the javaagent. The test verifies that both the CLIENT span and SERVER span are produced with correct parent-child relationships, which implicitly validates that instrumenter.end(...) is called in onAsyncResponse — otherwise the CLIENT span would never complete and be exported.

threads.body: The intention of `library-autoconfigure` modules is to provide automatic instrumentation that is activated by just adding the jar dependency. `library` instrumentations in contrast are activated manually either through code or configuration changes. Here you have typical library instrumentation code in an autoconfigure module which doesn't make sense to me. replies.body:
@laurit, thanks for the feedback.

The current design follows the same pattern as the existing `apache-dubbo-2.7` instrumentation, which also places `DubboTelemetry` + `DubboTelemetryBuilder` directly in its `library-autoconfigure` module without a separate `library` module.

SOFARPC has an `@Extension` + `@AutoActive` SPI mechanism (analogous to Dubbo's `@Activate`), so the `OpenTelemetryClientFilter`/`OpenTelemetryServerFilter` in `library-autoconfigure` are auto-discovered and activated by the framework — users just need to add the jar to their classpath with no code changes. I guess in practice there wouldn't be much demand for a separate `library` module where users would manually call `SofaRpcTelemetry.builder()...build().newClientFilter()` and register the filter themselves, since the SPI already handles that automatically.
  
Happy to split into `library` + `library-autoconfigure` if you think it's worth it.

`satisfiesAnyOf(...)` receives AssertJ assertion objects (e.g., `AbstractStringAssert<?>`) as lambda parameters. Wrapping them in `assertThat(val)` makes the assertions evaluate the assertion object itself, so these checks will never match and the test logic is broken. Use fluent assertions directly on the provided assert (`val.isNull()`, `val.isEqualTo(...)`).
